springer_source_data_probe._what: Springer Nature serves Source Data to a plain request with no login. The full MOESM asset space was enumerated by extension before any digitiser was written.
springer_source_data_probe.method: curl -o /dev/null -w %{http_code} over n = 1..16 x {xlsx, xls, zip, csv, docx, pdf, txt}; a 200 was then re-fetched and its first four bytes read. MAGIC BYTES, never a size floor.
springer_source_data_probe.result: n = 1,2,3,4 return 200 for .pdf ONLY (magic 25504446 = '%PDF'). n = 5..16 return 403 for every extension. NO extension of any n returned a 'PK' magic, so NO xlsx/zip workbook exists for this article.
springer_source_data_probe.cross_check: the article landing page's own 'Supplementary information' and 'Source data' sections list exactly four assets and name them: Supplementary Information (PDF), Reporting Summary (PDF), Source Data Fig. 1 (PDF, 'Sanger sequencing results'), Source Data Extended Data Fig. 1 (PDF, 'Uncropped gel image'). The enumeration and the page agree: four PDFs, no workbook.

author_repository_probe.command: python3 -I find_repo.py --doi 10.1038/s41587-026-03298-8 --pmid 42806111 --title 'Lipid nanoparticles large RNA' --author Dahlman
author_repository_probe.author_arg_note: the --author argument given to the tool was 'Dahlman'; the paper's group is Bowen Li (Toronto), not Dahlman. The DOI and PMID code searches do not depend on that argument and are what the conclusion rests on.
author_repository_probe.result: no author repository. The DOI and PMID code searches returned only third-party literature-aggregator repositories (e.g. jam-sudo/TrendBio, whose hits are scraped PubMed/RSS JSON dumps). The repo-name searches for the group returned 0. The paper's Data availability statement names no repository, no accession and no DOI: 'All other data supporting the findings of this study are available within the paper and its Supplementary Information or upon reasonable request.'
